payments for basic-income recipients and children, an energy allowance, and abolition of the EEG surcharge.","notes":["The excerpt says the packages were put into motion, not that they were fully launched or implemented."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E006","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"A January 2022 report described Scholz's planned Madrid visit with Pedro Sánchez as a gesture of social-democratic unity and reported that the leaders faced shared European economic-recovery and pandemic-related challenges.","notes":["The excerpt supports a gesture of unity, but not that Sánchez specifically sought cooperation with Scholz on those challenges."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E009","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"A 31 August 2022 report stated that Germany faced 7.9% inflation in August, a Bundesbank forecast of 10% in autumn, a 4.4% fall in real wages in the second quarter, dependence on Russian gas, disagreement over a gas surcharge and a third relief package, 25% approval for Scholz, and 62% dissatisfaction with the performance of his government and coalition.","notes":["The excerpt attributes the 62% figure to dissatisfaction with the performance of Scholz and the coalition, not simply government
